about: #4628: each surviving det-port mutant stated `equivalent` or `unreachable`, with the Java change and why it cannot alter observable behaviour; proposed in a PR, reviewed by the owner. A run that kills a stated mutant fails (the claim was wrong). Ids are mutation.py's; before / after are the Java line.

verdicts.equivalent: the change cannot alter anything the program shows (output, screen, files, COMMAREA, abend)
verdicts.unreachable: no input of the program reaches the changed code
verdicts.harness-gap: the change alters behaviour the proof runs but does not compare (open: the harness must)
verdicts.case-gap: an input the case lacks would kill it (open: strengthen the case)

survivors.reason: PROCESS-PAGE-BACKWARD is performed only from PROCESS-PF7-KEY, so EIBAID is always PF7 there: `NOT = DFHENTER AND DFHPF8` and `NOT = DFHENTER OR DFHPF8` are both true
WHEN OTHER's CONTINUE negated: the branch does nothing either way

survivors.reason: a symbolic-map subfield name mutant: `DetCics.subfields` reports attribute / colour / highlight / cursor for this field only when the program set one, and COUSR00C sets none for a list row field (its only cursor is USRIDIN), so no subfield event is emitted under either name

CURDATEI is overwritten by POPULATE-HEADER-INFO (MOVE ... TO CURDATEO, the same storage) before every SEND-USRLST-SCREEN, so the received value is never observable
READPREV's WHEN OTHER sets USRIDINL to -1, but READPREV is performed only from PROCESS-PAGE-BACKWARD, reached only from PROCESS-PF7-KEY, which has already moved -1 to USRIDINL
COUSR00C never reads EIBRESP (it has no RESP on ENDBR); the statement after it still tests the returned condition
